definition: A repository stores a project's files and the history of changes to them.
A clone is a local copy of a remote Git repository.
A commit records a set of file changes in a repository's history.
A branch is a named reference pointing to its latest commit.
A Git reference is a name, such as a branch or tag, that identifies a commit.
A Git tag gives a name to a particular commit in a repository's history.
A remote is a repository that a local Git repository connects to through a configured URL.
A push sends local commits to a remote repository.
A mirror clone is the bare local repository copy used to transfer an existing repository during migration.
Incremental migration transfers commits in chunks so a failed transfer can resume with the chunks that did not succeed.
A pull request proposes source branch changes for review before merging them into a destination branch.
An approval pool identifies the reviewers whose approvals count toward a pull request approval rule.
A destination reference selects the branch receiving changes when a template determines whether to create an approval rule.
An ARN uniquely identifies an AWS resource.
A role is an AWS identity whose permissions a caller can use by assuming it.
A role session is a temporary use of a role through the credentials issued when the caller assumes it.
Federation lets an identity authenticated outside AWS obtain access through an IAM role.
A credential helper supplies authentication information when Git connects to a repository.
A service role is a role an AWS service assumes to perform actions on your behalf.
A wildcard lets one pattern match multiple identity or branch names.
An event rule matches fields in an event and routes matching events to configured targets.
A repository trigger invokes Lambda or sends an SNS notification when selected repository operations occur.
A notification rule selects repository event types for notifications sent to its configured target.
A topic is a named communication channel used to distribute notifications to subscribers.
A webhook lets a supported source provider notify CodeBuild about repository activity that can start a build.
Temporary credentials authorize AWS access for a limited lifetime and stop working after they expire.
A policy defines permissions that determine which operations an identity can perform on a resource.
Encryption at rest protects repository data while CodeCommit stores it.
Encryption in transit protects repository data while HTTPS or SSH carries it between the client and CodeCommit.
Best-effort delivery attempts to send every service event to EventBridge but can occasionally leave an event undelivered.
